agent.problem: Too many of this stop's ten choices depend on luck or prior knowledge rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Cards 2, 3, 5, 8, 11, 12 and 14 ask for the angel, the extent of John's testimony, the scope of the blessing, the number of churches, sins, a kingdom and priests, or how many people will see Him without providing a basis for inferring those answers. These are not merely a few discovery questions among mostly informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: The fill-in-the-blank questions at stop 1 card 8, stop 1 card 11 and stop 2 card 7 use blanks for seven, sins and lampstands when the preceding cards provide no way to reason out those details. They test unrevealed wording rather than meaning the baker can infer.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

agent.problem: Many choice questions rely on antecedents or context absent from the question itself: stop 1 cards 14 and 15 use He and Him without naming Jesus, and card 17 refers to this new voice; stop 2 card 2 refers to all this, card 12 uses His with John as the nearest named person, card 13 refers to all of this, and cards 15 through 18 repeatedly use He or His without identifying the speaker. The baker has to reconstruct the subject from cards that are no longer visible.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: Two important parts of the passage are only approached through negation and are never actually taught. Stop 1 card 5 can be answered false without the baker learning that verse 3 also blesses those who hear and obey. Stop 2 card 17 can be answered false without presenting verse 19's three-part command; in particular, the things that are never appear on any card.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
